subject: RFP: Legal scenarios — IP assignment, indemnity flow, and order form notes
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: Legal scenarios — IP assignment, indemnity flow, and order form notes

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the list of scenario questions. Attached is our working draft that answers the legal questionnaire items you flagged (IP ownership vs. license, indemnity carve-outs, proposed liability cap ranges and the draft order form). Key highlights:

- IP: Redwood proposes standard model output license to the customer; we do not assign underlying model IP. For custom model work (if requested) we can address work-for-hire on a per-SOW basis.
- Indemnity: Redwood accepts third-party IP infringement indemnity limited to (i) claims arising from our models and (ii) our direct breach of license; we request reciprocal carve-outs for customer-provided prompt/content that causes claims.
- Liability cap: Our standard is subscription-based cap equal to 12 months of fees; for one-off professional services we propose a separate cap aligned to the SOW value.

Attachment: Redwood_RFP_Legal_Responses_v1.2.pdf (summary + annotated questionnaire), OrderForm_Draft_20260912.docx (draft order form with pricing and term options).

Request: Can you confirm whether NovaMed needs indemnity for data subject claims (i.e., claims alleging misuse of personal data in outputs) or whether that will be covered under separate security/compliance appendices? That answer will change our suggested language.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call tomorrow if you want to walk through.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of GTM Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

---

(Attachment stubs included: Redwood_RFP_Legal_Responses_v1.2.pdf, OrderForm_Draft_20260912.docx)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novamed.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Grant <m.grant@novamed.com>, procurement_rfp@novamed.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Legal scenarios — IP assignment, indemnity flow, and order form notes

Stephanie —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear breakdown. A few items NovaMed needs clarification on before we circulate to legal:

1) Data-related claims: yes, we require indemnity for third-party claims that directly result from Redwood processing NovaMed personal data and producing outputs that cause harm. We understand the sensitivity and are open to narrow language that requires (a) Redwood to have followed agreed processing controls and (b) a material breach to have occurred.
2) IP and custom dev: for custom model development we expect assignment of deliverables (customer-owned training artifacts and derivative models). Is Redwood able to commit to assignment for deliverables only (not the base model weights)?
3) Liability cap: our legal team will push for a cap at 24 months' fees for enterprise contracts with data processing. Can you indicate whether Redwood will consider increasing the cap if we add enhanced SLAs and higher pricing?

Also attached is a short redline from our procurement counsel to the order form (we will send formal redline before end of day). Can you get internal confirmation on the data indemnity ask and assignment carve?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Director, Strategic Sourcing
NovaMed Systems

---

(Email includes reference to an incoming redline attachment from NovaMed; procurement_rfp@novamed.com to receive formal redline.)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: RFP: Legal scenarios — quick internal notes

Looping in Laura with procurement/legal negotiation context. Short notes to feed into our response to NovaMed: 

- On data-related indemnity: we can accept a narrow indemnity tied to Redwood's breach of our Data Processing Addendum controls. Proposed wording: "Redwood will indemnify NovaMed against third-party claims arising directly from Redwood's failure to comply with the DPA and resulting in personal data misuse, provided NovaMed reasonably cooperates in defense." This keeps exposure limited.

- On assignment for custom work: we can agree to assignment of customer-specific deliverables (trained artifacts, fine-tuned model checkpoints created solely from NovaMed data) while explicitly reserving pre-existing model weights and optimizer/training pipelines. That aligns with precedent.

- Liability cap: raising cap to 24 months is possible but requires (a) premium pricing tier and (b) a negotiated SLA schedule (availability and response times). Suggest we prepare two order form options: Standard (12 months cap) and Enterprise+ (24 months cap + SLA bundle + extended indemnity with higher limits).

Action: Stephanie — can you fold these proposals into a v1.3 and call out the lines that are flexible vs. non-negotiable? I can join the sync with NovaMed's procurement if needed.

-Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---

(Internal forwarded message. No attachments in this internal note.)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Legal scenarios — IP assignment, indemnity flow, and order form notes

Samantha —

Thanks for the feedback and the redline. We spoke internally and updated our draft to reflect the following compromises (see attached v1.3):

- Data indemnity: Redwood will indemnify NovaMed for third-party claims arising from Redwood's failure to comply with the DPA controls, subject to customary notice/cooperation clauses and a requirement that NovaMed not materially alter prompts or customer data flows in a way that creates claim exposure.
- Custom deliverables assignment: Redwood will assign ownership of customer-produced deliverables (fine-tuned models and training artifacts derived solely from NovaMed inputs). Redwood expressly retains ownership of base model weights, training code, and underlying model IP.
- Liability cap options: included two order form options — (i) Standard: 12 months of fees cap; (ii) Enterprise+: 24 months of fees cap with SLA bundle and premium pricing. Language in the order form flags which fields trigger the Enterprise+ pricing.

Attached: Redwood_RFP_Legal_Responses_v1.3.pdf (redlines accept/decline summary), OrderForm_Draft_20260915.docx (two-tier order form).

Next steps: if NovaMed legal accepts the DPA-tied data indemnity and the assignment carve for deliverables, we can proceed to a commercial redline pass and a short exec call to finalize pricing tier.

Happy to schedule a 30-min call this week — Ben, can you propose times?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of GTM Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
